scope: Primary AOSP public API and internal stack source review only; no Bluetooth access
apple_lead: Root observed locationd CBConnectPeripheralOptionUseTempLTK with SearchParty connection token before FD44 GATT writes.

findings.finding: Public BluetoothDevice.connectGatt overloads have no encryption LTK input, and reviewed public API file exposes no LTK injection setter. GATT write authentication retry flags select security policy, not key bytes.
SystemApi LeBuilder.setLeTemporaryKey takes pairing TK for the LE Security Manager. It does not document an arbitrary LTK encrypted-connect equivalent.
createBond with non-null OOB data invokes enforceBluetoothPrivilegedPermissionIfNeeded, requiring BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED. WSS grant does not grant this permission.
Internal btm_ble_start_encrypt uses a supplied STK or stored peer LTK and invokes HCI encryption. This native stack function is not exposed as an ordinary APK API in reviewed sources.

conclusion: If Apple requires token-derived temporary LTK encryption before FD44 discovery/writes, plain public Android GATT cannot express that step using the verified API surface. A Samsung UWB vendor helper alone does not solve BLE encryption setup. A separate equivalent vendor/system endpoint remains unverified.
limitations: Reviewed upstream source may differ from Samsung phone Bluetooth framework
No attempt to insert keys, alter bonds, invoke hidden APIs or bypass access controls
Not claiming Apple temporary LTK equals Bluetooth legacy pairing TK or ordinary STK
